boundary_rationale: אִם לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.8, tier: byte) opens this unit: the negation sits on אִם לֹ֤א ('if not'), and תֵדְעִי֙ itself carries second-feminine-singular marking ('you know') rather than the opening token, a grammatical-gender flip from the second-masculine address of Song.1.7 that signals a new speaker. The feminine imperatives צְֽאִי and וּרְעִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.8, tier: byte, 'go out' / 'graze') hold one addressee (her); inside the span's own bytes, רַעְיָתִֽי (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte, 'my love'), his tier-1 address anchor for her (sweep: 9 verses), secures the male-voice attribution for this span alongside the 2fs object suffix on דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte, 'I have compared you'). The second-feminine-singular suffixes continue through לְחָיַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Song.1.10, tier: byte, 'your cheeks') and לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte, the 2fs dative in 'we will make for you'), holding one addressee across all four verses with no further gender-marked interruption: “Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.” (web:Song.1.10) and “We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.” (web:Song.1.11).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off Song.1.11's cohortative 'we will make you earrings' into its own unit was rejected: the person shift from singular to plural carries no accompanying gender-marked addressee change, and the second-feminine-singular 'you' target continues unbroken from Song.1.8-Song.1.10.

device_notes: Song.1.11's cohortative 'we will make' could in principle mark a third voice (companions) joining the man's praise rather than a majestic-plural extension of his own; no tier-1 gender-marked form distinguishes a new speaker there, so it is held inside this unit and the ambiguity is disclosed rather than resolved. A setumah sits at Song.1.8 in the WLC parashah layer (single-witness; tier-3 corroboration only) at the verse that opens this unit.

boundary_rationale: This span is held as one antiphonal bracket rather than atomized per line: הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.15, tier: byte, 'behold you are beautiful, my love') opens in the man's voice, using his word for her in the final token; הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte, 'behold you are beautiful, my beloved') answers with the mirrored formula and her word for him, confirming the reply is hers, and her turn continues through קֹר֤וֹת בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ אֲרָזִ֔ים (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte, 'the beams of our house are cedars') with the 1cp form עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte, 'our couch') and בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte, 'our house') continuing her plural possessive with no gender-marked interruption; the verse's other 1cp noun stands as a ketiv/qere pair, ketiv רחיטנו against the qere רַהִיטֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte, 'our rafters'), disclosed here rather than claimed at either reading. Song.2.1's self-description אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת (oshb:Song.2.1, tier: byte, 'I am a rose') carries no gender-marked form and is held rather than attributed. The same mirrored alternation recurs at the far end of the span: כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.2, tier: byte, 'so [is] my love') is his line, and כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte, 'so [is] my beloved') is hers, closing the antiphon's second mirrored pair. The bytes run on past this close in the same first-person voice -- חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) continuing into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה (oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte) -- with no vocative, no address-vocabulary token, and no gender-marked addressee change at the cut, so the boundary at Song.2.3|Song.2.4 is not itself a voice-shift; it is held because the antiphon's own formal marker, the mirrored address pairs, completes at Song.2.2-Song.2.3, while Song.2.4 onward carries none. The closing seam is carried by bracket completion, a tier-1 driver class standing alongside voice-shift markers: the unit opens on the mirrored address pair הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.15, tier: byte) answered by הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte) and closes on the second mirrored address pair כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.2, tier: byte) answered by כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte). The two pairs are a structural mirror, not a byte-identical inclusio -- the opening and closing frames share no run -- and the gendered contrast that distinguishes the pair, הִנָּ֤ךְ against הִנְּךָ֨, is a byte-tier fact only: the two forms share a skeleton (word-bound sweep: 3 verses book-wide), so the contrast does not survive at skeleton tier. Confidence is held at medium_low.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the exchange through Song.2.4-Song.2.6 to the Song.2.7 adjuration close was considered and engaged from the bytes: the same first-person speaker configuration continues at byte tier past this span's own closing seam (חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי at oshb:Song.2.3 running into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה at oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte, both sides), yet it is rejected as the unit's own close because Song.2.4-Song.2.6 carries no antiphonal address-marker at all -- no vocative, no rayati/dodi term, no gendered second-person form -- while this span's own bracket is built entirely from the mirrored hinnakh/hinnekha and rayati/dodi address pairs that close formally at Song.2.2-Song.2.3. A re-cut variant, severing the run so it is not split across the boundary, was also considered and is unavailable at row granularity: spans are verse-granular, so Song.2.3 must fall wholly to one side, and that side carries the antiphon's closing anchor.

The two pairs are a structural mirror, not a byte-identical inclusio -- the opening and closing frames share no run -- and the gendered contrast that distinguishes the pair, הִנָּ֤ךְ against הִנְּךָ֨, is a byte-tier fact only: the two forms share a skeleton (word-bound sweep: 3 verses book-wide), so the contrast does not survive at skeleton tier. From Song.2.4 the unit is her continuing first-person voice on a new topic (the banquet hall), opened by וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה (oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte, 'and his banner over me is love') and carrying an addressed plural imperative at its own middle verse -- סַמְּכ֨וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי (oshb:Song.2.5, tier: byte, 'sustain me with raisins, refresh me'), two plural imperatives with first-person-singular object suffixes -- so the unit is not addressee-free; the same plural-imperative-addressee feature is what drives the cut at Song.2.15. The unit closes on the embrace colon quoted from the bytes rather than in translation: וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte, 'and his right hand embraces me'), attested in that witness as “His right hand embraces me.” (web:Song.2.6), immediately before the adjuration formula breaks in at Song.2.7.

The embrace colon's sub-runs שְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ תַּ֣חַת and וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte) recur at MT 8:3 (sweep: 2 verses); the colon is not identical across the two verses even at skeleton tier, since the lamed of לְרֹאשִׁ֔י (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte) is present here and absent from רֹאשִׁ֔י (oshb:Song.8.3, tier: byte) -- the recurrence stands at MT 8:3, immediately before the MT 8:4 adjuration, a parallel supporting this unit's own 2:6|2:7 close rather than a rival to it.

boundary_rationale: דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, tier: byte, 'my beloved is mine, and I am his') is the first of three attested mutual-belonging shapes in the book (sweep: 3 verses), in the his-mine order; Song.2.17 continues in the same first-person voice, held as tier-2 single-speaker corroboration alongside the mutual-belonging formula site rather than on any addressee-free ground. Within Song.2.17 itself the address turns second-masculine-singular: סֹב֩ דְּמֵה לְךָ֨ דוֹדִ֜י (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte, 'turn, be like, my beloved'), the final-kaf-plus-qamats suffix on לְךָ֨ contrasting with the final-kaf-plus-sheva second-feminine-singular suffix on מַרְאַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Song.2.14, tier: byte, 'your face'); the unit's own texture therefore carries an addressed imperative, not an interruption-free run, and the same feature drives the cut at Song.2.15. The unit closes on “Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.” (web:Song.2.17).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Song.2.16 from Song.2.17 at the mutual-belonging couplet was rejected: no addressee or gender-marked shift interrupts the run, and the couplet with the closing turn-imperative share one first-person voice.
